accepted_units.title: Prime-log resonance creates a lower-order bias beneath uniform distribution
accepted_units.why_material: Starts from uniform distribution of fractional parts of scaled zero ordinates, then identifies a second term of order T for smooth tests only when the scale is a rational multiple of a prime logarithm; the explicit periodic function g_alpha records that arithmetic resonance.
accepted_units.context_note: The affiliation block and page header interrupt the span but the setup must include both the uniform main term and the resonant definition; the interval-indicator boundary is deferred to the next unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Verify equations (1.1)-(1.4), the rational normalization of alpha, Fourier series, real-part sign, and smoothness classes against the arXiv PDF; prose and logic are high-confidence.

accepted_units.title: Interval counts would expose the bias through sharp discrepancy asymptotics
accepted_units.why_material: Moves from smooth test functions to interval indicators, defines discrepancy as a supremum over intervals, and records the precise conjectured first lower-order term together with the fact that RH alone does not establish it.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps the known unconditional and RH discrepancy estimates because they distinguish established scale from the proposed sharp term.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Original PDF required for the supremum, absolute value, normalization by N(T), and little-o scale in Conjectures 1-2.

accepted_units.title: The predicted bias gives a one-sided lower bound while RH leaves an alpha-dependent error
accepted_units.why_material: States the paper's unconditional discrepancy lower bound and its RH-conditioned interval-count inequality, showing exactly which half of the conjectured behavior is currently forced and what residual size remains.
accepted_units.context_note: This is retained separately from its smoothing proof so the established result is not conflated with the stronger conjectures.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Verify absolute values, supremum, sign, alpha/2 term, and normalization in Theorem 1 against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Uniform cancellation of zero exponential sums would upgrade smooth tests to intervals
accepted_units.why_material: Identifies sums of x to the i-gamma as the Fourier quantities controlling interval counts, formulates their required uniform cancellation range, proves that range sufficient under RH, and compares it with what Landau's formula and zero-density estimates already provide.
accepted_units.context_note: The exact lower x-range is part of the mechanism because later trigonometric truncation is chosen to fit it.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula risk: check (1.5)-(1.6), nearest-prime-power term, exponent ranges, and RH normalization against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: The explicit formula translates zero cancellation into prime regularity in short intervals
accepted_units.why_material: States a short-interval prime conjecture sufficient for the zero-sum conjecture and a converse implication with a weaker error, then contrasts both with a Gaussian fluctuation heuristic and known RH bounds.
accepted_units.context_note: The Gonek comparison is retained as a separate sufficient zero-sum hypothesis for the stronger square-root-style prime fluctuation claim, not treated as proved here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Verify every y-range, exponent, logarithmic factor, and implication direction in Conjecture 4, Theorem 3, (1.7), and the Gonek bound.

accepted_units.title: A weighted two-zero energy can certify one-frequency cancellation
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces the pair-correlation function as a quadratic representation of zero spacings, formulates the strengthened uniform asymptotic actually needed below the classical Montgomery range, and shows it implies the same zero-sum and discrepancy conjectures.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps the comparison with Montgomery's original range and Chan's stronger error so the source's Conjecture 5 is not mislabeled as standard pair correlation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Verify the kernel 4/(4+(gamma-gamma')^2), x phase, lower x-range, error size, and uniformity ranges in (1.8), Conjecture 5, and the remarks.

accepted_units.title: Positive smoothing converts the smooth-test asymptotic into an interval discrepancy witness
accepted_units.why_material: Convolves a maximizing interval indicator with a nonnegative approximate identity, applies the known smooth asymptotic, uses boundedness of g_alpha under a small translate, and extracts at least one shifted interval realizing the lower bound.
accepted_units.context_note: The choice of a maximizing interval and the final epsilon limit are essential; this proves only the one-sided lower bound.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Verify convolution orientation, normalization, translated interval, inequality sign, and O(epsilon T) term against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Extremal trigonometric polynomials sandwich an interval with controlled Fourier cost

accepted_units.title: Resonant Fourier modes reproduce g_alpha while nonresonant modes average away
accepted_units.why_material: Expands the polynomial counts into zero exponential sums, applies Landau's formula frequency by frequency, identifies prime-power modes exactly when alpha is resonant, and proves uniform convergence makes every other mode o(T); this derives the source's bias rather than assuming it.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Arithmetic resonance is discovered by Fourier selection, not added as a correction by hand
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Approximating an interval by controlled Fourier modes and inserting Landau's formula separates prime-power frequencies from all other modes; the surviving modes assemble exactly into g_alpha and explain the lower-order nonuniformity.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The sharp interval asymptotic still needs uniform control of the unresolved high-frequency tail, and all exact Fourier/Landau formulas require PDF verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Three dual channels constrain the same zero exponential sum
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The linear statistic needed for sharp fractional-part counts can be controlled either from local prime-counting regularity through the explicit formula or from a quadratic pair-correlation energy through smoothing; both routes target the same cancellation but expose different sufficient information.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The paper proves conditional implications, not an unconditional equivalence among all three conjectural packages, and the pair-correlation input is stronger and extends below Montgomery's classical range.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Changing the test representation relocates the regularity obstruction
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Positive convolution is enough to extract a one-sided discrepancy witness, while two-sided sharp interval counts require extremal or band-limited representations whose approximation loss and Fourier tail can both be quantified.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Smoothing does not prove the full indicator conjecture, and the optimized polynomial loss cannot remove the need for new zero-sum information.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The Selberg-class transfer succeeds until degree moves the correlation transition
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The analytic/Euler-product axioms, zero-density estimate, and generalized Landau formula carry the fractional-part and short-interval mechanisms to primitive L-functions, but degree shifts the natural pair-correlation transition beyond the formula's effective range and forces a new smooth-transition hypothesis.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a conditional extension within the stated Selberg-class hypotheses; the source neither proves the transition regularity nor resolves the degree-at-least-two obstruction.

within_source_saturation: Whole-source saturation was reached after first-to-last inspection. The 23 accepted units cover each distinct definition, conjectural bridge, theorem strength, approximation construction, explicit-formula mechanism, pair-correlation energy argument, Selberg-class transfer, and stated degree obstruction. The only unsegmented material is title/page furniture, repeated abstract-level summary, finite plot pixels already linked as supporting context, acknowledgement, and bibliography; formula typography remains an attached PDF-verification dependency rather than mathematics reconstructed from memory.
stop_reason: Segmentation stopped only after all lines 1-1171 were exactly classified and the complete mathematical progression was represented: resonant lower-order bias, interval/discrepancy barriers, zero-sum links to primes and pair correlation, all three proof mechanisms, and the general L-function extension with its degree transition failure. Further units would duplicate these mechanisms or select page furniture, plots without additional argument, or references; no source quota or batch limit was used.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter, abstract, and four-part program
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Identifies the source and states its goals: define Lehmer pairs, turn them into lower bounds for the de Bruijn-Newman constant, prove existence, and compute improved bounds.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Heat-flow family and phase boundary
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Relates the xi transform to H_t, defines the de Bruijn-Newman phase boundary and Laguerre-Polya characterization, and supplies Hadamard zero coordinates.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Lehmer-pair criterion and main theorem
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Turns Lehmer's near counterexample into a gap-plus-global-environment criterion, states the pair-specific lower bound and infinite-pair consequence, and previews two numerical applications.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Local zero motion and collision
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives the velocity of a simple real zero, interprets pair collision as a lower-bound witness, and uses Laguerre inequalities/backward heat flow to place multiple zeros at or below the phase boundary.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Zero-motion ODE and interaction bounds
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses Hadamard factorization to express zero velocity and gap evolution through interactions with other zeros, then derives differential control for an auxiliary interaction sum.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Proofs of the pair theorem and infinite-pair corollary
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Solves the squared-gap differential inequality by an integrating factor, obtains a contradiction before the candidate collision time, and takes a vanishing-gap limit.

sections_inspected.label: 4. Global moment and finite-tail certification
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Computes the total reciprocal-square zero moment from Taylor coefficients and bounds the error in replacing the global interaction by finitely many zeros.

sections_inspected.label: 4. Lehmer's pair and its lower bound
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Certifies the classical close pair as a Lehmer pair, converts it into a lower bound, and tests sensitivity to deliberately coarse interaction estimates.

sections_inspected.label: 5. Later record pair and stronger lower bound
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Explains the record-gap search rule, certifies a much later pair with a local window plus tail bounds, and obtains the paper's strongest lower bound and continuation heuristic.
